F8 (test_lint audit round 2, task t30554): TestRecordReferences._collect_reference now also scans <menuitem> parent=/action=/groups= xmlid references (convert.py's _tag_menuitem resolves all three via id_get/env.ref, raise_if_not_found=True by default), where the previous scan only checked <field ref=...>/eval/t-value. This surfaced 2 real pre-existing dangling refs, both action= attributes naming a nonexistent xmlid 'ir_cron_scheduler_action_ir_actions_server' (real record is stock.ir_cron_scheduler_action, an ir.cron): addons/stock/views/stock_menus.xml:179 and addons/mrp/views/mrp_menus.xml:69. Both are outside this audit's scope (odoo/addons/test_lint only), so left unedited and filed as task t30555 (EO2.4.420) rather than silently fixed here. Measured via: odoo-bin --addons-path=odoo/addons,addons -d tl_audit_r2 --test-enable --test-tags /test_lint:TestRecordReferences --stop-after-init --no-http --db_maxconn 8.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

STAMP REFRESHED AFTER THE REBASE, NUMBER UNCHANGED. Same reasoning as bundle_double_eval: enforced through test_lint's assert_ratchet, which does not consult the stamp, so the orphaned flag was a reporting problem rather than an enforcement one. TestRecordReferences ran in the same CI-scope run -- eight of its methods are in the log by name -- and passed under an exact ratchet, which pins the count at 0.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

Re-measured at 24f92b0f744 after a rebase orphaned the previous stamp ba8fa548493; count unchanged (0). Measured on a clean detached worktree of that commit through the test_lint lane's own reader: odoo-bin --addons-path=odoo/addons,addons -i test_lint --test-enable --test-tags /test_lint on a fresh database, where test_record_refs held at the floor.

All 8 banked findings were false positives, in three classes the checker did not model, each verified against the ORM path that resolves the ref. (1) <record forcecreate="False"> makes convert.py call id_get(raise_if_not_found=False), so a missing xmlid yields False instead of failing the install -- 4 refs in point_of_sale/data/orders_demo.xml and pos_restaurant. (2) ref("xmlid", False) passes the same flag explicitly -- website_event_sale and website_event_track, both under a comment reading "Update the event type if exists". (3) An xmlid minted in Python through a helper call rather than a bare literal: pos_restaurant mints pos_config_main_restaurant via _get_suffixed_ref_name(), which the scan already intended to catch -- its own comment names pos_restaurant -- but the regex required the literal to follow the colon directly. The gate asserts a missing xmlid stops a module loading; for all 8 it cannot, so the number meant something other than its own message. Checker corrected in the same change; measured 10 -> 1 -> 0 as each class was modelled.
